title: Whether the suite's green is also a fact about collection order
note: D-2026-63. tests/ has no __init__.py, so pytest puts tests/ on sys.path and not the repository root; 103 of 106 modules insert the root themselves and three did not. Those three passed every full run because the alphabet put a module that inserts it first, and failed on their own. I1 removes the structural guarantee the conftest provides and the three go back to depending on what ran before them. I2-I5 attack the tool that keeps it closed: the empty scope it must refuse, the failure it must report, the count that makes its scope visible, and the exit code it must read instead of the output text.

mutations.name: I1_the_conftest_stops_putting_the_root_on_the_path
mutations.rationale: the file still exists and still imports, so every check that reads it passes; the three modules that carry no insert of their own go back to importing only when something else has run first

mutations.name: I2_an_empty_scope_is_agreed_with
mutations.rationale: 'every module collects alone' becomes a statement about no modules, which is what a moved directory or a changed glob produces

mutations.name: I3_a_module_that_cannot_be_collected_is_not_reported
mutations.rationale: the tool runs every collection, watches them fail and reports that collection order is not load-bearing

mutations.name: I4_the_tool_stops_saying_how_many_it_checked
mutations.find: print(f"{len(found) - len(broken)} of {len(found)} test modules can be "
mutations.rationale: a verdict without its scope: a run that checked three modules and one that checked a hundred and six read identically

mutations.name: I5_a_collection_failure_is_read_off_the_text_instead_of_the_exit_code
mutations.rationale: the proxy again -- a substring standing in for the property. Every collection failure that is not a missing module (a SyntaxError, a fixture error, a timeout) is then reported as a module that collects perfectly well
